title: Inference of a universal social scale and segregation measures using social connectivity kernels
benchmark_measurement: Measurement of social homophily and segregation based on religious affiliation differences.
findings: Religious differences contribute to social segregation, with homophily observed in friendship networks. In the US General Social Survey dataset, having a different religion had a negative effect on the odds of forming a social connection, equivalent to a seven-year age difference. However, the contribution of religion to overall social segregation was found to be smaller than that of physical distance and age.
